_comment: WC2026 Round of 32. KNOCKOUT: no draw -- level after 90' -> extra time -> penalties, so the deliverable is who ADVANCES. Routes: Australia finished 2nd in Group D (2-0 Turkey, 0-2 USA, 0-0 Paraguay; 4 pts, GF 2 GA 2, GD 0, rating 75) -- a DEFENSIVE, low-scoring, organized grinder (scored in only one game, two of three were 0-goal outputs). Egypt came through Group G (1-1 Belgium, 3-1 New Zealand, 1-1 Iran; 5 pts, GF 5 GA 3, GD +2, rating 74) -- organized and solid, HELD Belgium 1-1 and drew Iran, decent at the back. Ratings are essentially EQUAL (75 vs 74) -> a coin-flip tie. KEY texture: this is the TIGHT, low-block archetype -- BOTH sides are organized and low-scoring, NOT open/leaky -> a cagey, low-total game (1-0/0-0/1-1 shape) with HIGH extra-time/penalty risk, the opposite of the open ties (USA-Bosnia, Switzerland-Algeria). KNOCKOUT CAUTION APPLIED (see results_log standing note): kept total xG low (~2.0), BTTS-No favoured, clean-sheet probabilities high -- do NOT over-lean BTTS-Yes here; two cautious sides focused on not making mistakes. Egypt the marginal favourite by underlying quality (held Belgium) despite Australia's nominal home; near 50/50. Home = Australia (nominal; neutral venue). Cards not modelled (referee TBD).

_postmatch.result: Australia 1-1 Egypt (after extra time), Egypt won on PENALTIES. The tight tie went the distance and Egypt -- the marginal favourite -- advance to the Round of 16 (where they meet the Argentina-Cape Verde winner).
_postmatch.model_1x2: Australia 31.8 / Draw 32.7 / Egypt 35.5 (LOW, 90'); advancement Australia 47.9 / Egypt 52.1
_postmatch.verdict: Textbook process hit on BOTH the texture and the side -- as good as this archetype gets. I called this a near coin-flip between two organized, low-scoring sides (LOW confidence, 'no strong read'), with the TIGHT low-block texture: total xG 2.03, the 1-1 the single most likely scoreline (14.6%), 0-0 second (14.2%), BTTS-No 58%, and -- crucially -- the HIGHEST extra-time/penalty risk of the whole round (ET 32.7%, pens 18.9%). Result: 1-1, into extra time, decided on PENALTIES. That is the model's central scenario landing almost exactly. And the ADVANCEMENT side was right too: Egypt, the marginal favourite (52.1%), won the shootout and advanced -- the ~50/50 that tipped the pick's way. The knockout-caution note paid off here: leaning the goals texture DOWN (not the open both-score read) matched a 1-1 grind perfectly.
_postmatch.lesson: The tight, two-organized-sides archetype is the penalty-lottery zone -- correctly flagged (highest pens% in the round) and it delivered a shootout. When the model has NO strong 1X2 read (LOW, near coin-flip), the honest deliverable is exactly that: 'this is 50/50 and likely to go deep', and the advancement split (52/48) is the real content, not a confident pick. Egypt winning the coin-flip is the process working: the marginal favourite advanced, but a kick either way (like Germany/Netherlands losing theirs) would NOT have been a process error -- the shootout is near-random by design. Knockout caution (low goals texture) was validated a third time, now including the tight-tie direction (1-1), not just the favourite-clean-sheet direction.
